svg.title: The experiment and what it measures. Control is the existing product page; treatment is the product page plus Nykaa Fit, enabled only for women's dresses. Primary metric: product view to add to bag conversion. The business metric it serves: the share of users who buy at least one wishlisted item within 30 days of saving it. Assignment is a deterministic FNV 1a hash of a persisted randomisation unit, so a visitor always lands in the same arm. TREATMENT_ALLOCATION is the only dial: 0 everyone control, 0.5 a live test, 1 everyone treatment, the dev default; override with ?fit=on or ?fit=off or from /fit-lab. 17 events go through one analytics abstraction with pluggable sinks. /metrics maps them onto nine metrics: profile started, profile completed, recommendation shown, recommendation followed, size selected, added to bag, wishlist item resolved, order placed, return reported. Guardrails enforced by tests: body measurements never enter an event, and the engine cannot import the review corpus or a body estimator. The Fit Lab withholds rates below a display floor: 1 of 1 is shown as a count, never as 100%.

section.h2: Built to be measured, not to look good.
section.p: The business metric: the share of users who buy at least one wishlisted item within 30 days of saving it. A wishlist is a queue of unresolved questions, and “will this fit?” is the one that never resolves on its own.

div.p: TREATMENT_ALLOCATION is the only dial. Deterministic FNV 1a hash, so a visitor always lands in the same arm. Primary metric: product view to add to bag.
Pluggable sinks, localStorage by default. registerSink() connects a real provider without touching a call site.

div.div: No body in the dataMeasurements never enter an event. A test checks every event the app can emit.
No borrowed opinionsA test walks every engine file and fails on any import of the review corpus or a body estimator.
No fake ratesThe Fit Lab withholds rates below a display floor: “1 of 1” is a count, never 100%.
